taskDescription: Arrange the steps of duodenal iron absorption in the correct order, from dietary iron in the gut lumen to transferrin-bound iron in the blood.

sequenceImages.imageDescription: Dietary ferric iron (Fe³⁺) in the duodenal lumen
Dcytb reduces Fe³⁺ to Fe²⁺ at the brush border, aided by vitamin C
DMT1 transports Fe²⁺ across the apical membrane into the enterocyte
Ferroportin exports iron across the basolateral membrane
Hephaestin oxidises Fe²⁺ to Fe³⁺, which binds transferrin in the blood

l10n.score: You got @score of @total points. Iron absorption follows a fixed duodenal sequence — luminal Fe³⁺ is reduced (Dcytb + vitamin C), enters the enterocyte (DMT1), is exported basolaterally (ferroportin, the hepcidin target), re-oxidised (hephaestin) and loaded onto transferrin — each protein is a potential point of regulation or disease.
